itemDispositions.reasoning: Opened packages/shared/src/rules/encounter-difficulty.ts, its tests, the rendered client labels, and docs/guides/change-rules-logic.md. The module attributes the calculator to the 2024 DMG and names only Low, Moderate, and High thresholds at lines 2-8, but places "trivial" beside those terms at line 14 and assigns every below-Low encounter to it at lines 93-97. The client presents that term without qualification, and the policy-protecting test also omits the repository-required Musi-policy classification.

Opened packages/shared/src/schemas/homebrew-campaign.ts:5-11, packages/shared/src/schemas/inventory.ts:116-118, packages/shared/src/schemas/auth.ts:64-72, and the router return sites. The weaker boolean acknowledgments are real, but authored leaf 194 exactly covers these three declarations, their literal-true producers, and convergence on successResponseSchema. No residual remains.

Opened both shared input modules and traced their production consumers. spell-casting-inputs.ts:29-45 uses spellLevel for ordinary use and recovery, matching CharacterSpellSlot terminology. sorcery-point-inputs.ts:10-43 consistently uses slotLevel for Flexible Casting's selected slot and result. The names change at an intentional domain boundary and are internally consistent; renaming public inputs would be churn without demonstrated ambiguity.

Opened packages/shared/src/map/drawing.ts, packages/shared/src/map/fog.ts, and the shared package export map, then searched non-test consumers for DrawingShapeType, FreehandShape, LineShape, RectangleShape, CircleShape, and isCellVisible. They have no internal production adopters, but the five aliases are deliberately schema-paired inferred names on the public ./map/*.js surface. isCellVisible is a focused documented helper with substantial direct coverage. Monorepo non-use alone does not establish accidental dead code worth a leaf.

Opened the four adjacent initiative-tracker suites and the shared encounter fixture. initiative-row.test.tsx:29-44, initiative-row-info.test.tsx:41-56, initiative-row-actions.test.tsx:24-39, and dm-participant-tools.test.tsx:16-31 repeat the same participant scenario, including identity, HP, AC, initiative, and challenge-rating defaults. fixtures-encounter.ts:7-44 supplies structural defaults but not this repeated combat scenario, leaving four synchronized maintenance sites.

Opened scripts/drift-triage/triage-packets.test.ts around its fixture setup and boundary cases. The suite already has a general typed item builder at lines 6-17. The local boundaryItem/build pairs at 365-379, 395-409, and 476-490 differ in arity, ID construction, cited range, and source bytes and sit beside comments explaining exclusive-end, caret, and UTF-8 semantics. Parameterizing those differences would obscure more than it removes.

Opened vitest.slow.config.ts and comparable root-pinning code. vitest.slow.config.ts:22 feeds URL.pathname directly to node:path, retaining percent escapes and producing URL-style Windows drive paths before lines 27-55 join package roots. Comparable configs and E2E helpers use fileURLToPath(import.meta.url), so this is a real portability defect in the only config that runs the slow tier.

Opened toast-provider.test.tsx and toast-provider.tsx. The first case at test lines 8-16 only checks that Testing Library returned a container; the second at 18-26 renders the same provider and meaningfully proves child passthrough. Removing the redundant smoke case is valid housekeeping, but the production component is only seven lines and the deletion has no material maintenance mechanism warranting a standalone leaf.

Opened docs/generated/lint-coverage-map.md and its parser/suggestion code. The document declares itself a current resolved inventory at lines 3-17, while the Leaf-41 section is visibly implementation history and records what landed, what remains, and that no pending-leaf rows remain at lines 458-486. The proposed/pending-leaf vocabulary remains part of the active parser and suggestion contracts. This is provenance, not a false current task.

Opened all four external-invocation spans in scripts/drift-ai/README.md:18-72, 120-134, 235-300, and 628-685. The repetition is real but is already exactly and exhaustively authored as leaf 086, including the four narratives and audience split. No novel residual exists.

Opened the comments and live command wiring. config.ts:116-121 says no subcommand or advisory reads coverage artifacts, while prototype-subcommands.ts:49-60 registers two such commands and coverage-unused-correlation-command.ts:46-69 consumes the artifacts. clone-candidates.ts:5-10 and class-construction.ts:1-6 likewise deny CLI/advisory surfaces that the same registry now exposes. These are current-state falsities in modules maintainers open for ownership guidance.

Opened docs/ai-harness.md:656-659 and 694-709, .github/workflows/slow-drift.yml:43-49, and scripts/slow-drift-audit.sh:323-412. The contradiction is real, but authored leaf 223 exactly covers removing the fulfilled shared-rules mutation gap and reviewing the adjacent timing claim. No residual remains.

Opened the canonical shared schemas and their production copies. abilityAbbreviationSchema defines six values, but SAVE_ABILITIES and several client surfaces repeat them. More materially, spellSchoolSchema owns eight schools while the homebrew editor maintains a second inventory and Set; parseSchool silently converts anything absent from that copy to evocation. Neighboring spell UI already derives options from spellSchoolSchema.options, proving the intended single-source idiom.

Opened packages/shared/src/schemas/spell.ts:83-121, packages/server/src/utils/spell-mapping.ts:16-18 and 37-38, resolve-character-spell.ts:86-101, and the general dice parser. The duplication is four statements across two tightly coupled consumers of one already-validated bare-formula contract. The adjacent parseDiceNotation handles a materially broader grammar; a new narrow public helper for two trivial consumers would be disproportionate. The cut's CQ25-179 grammar premise is inaccurate, but the cleanup remains too small for a leaf.

Opened the seeded AC glossary, shared calculator and tests, sheet calculation, persisted stats, and encounter projection. The rule requires choosing among alternative base-AC calculations, but computeCharacterAc stops at the first matching class. Its test pins an order-dependent Barbarian/Monk result of 13 even though Monk alone yields 15. The absent persisted preference and split AC authorities make the fix nontrivial, but they do not negate the user-visible rules mismatch.

Opened the level-up schemas, Prisma model, apply-level-up mutations, router surface, architecture wording, and leaves 192 and 217. CharacterLevelChoice stores selected new metadata, while level-up mutates stats, class rows, feats, features, sorcery, subclass, and slots without prior-state snapshots, inverse operations, transaction grouping, or safe handling of later edits. Leaf 217 correctly removes the unsupported rollback claim; implementing undo is a separate large product and persistence design, not a bounded missing implementation.

Opened the shared codemod fixture runner, its four suite consumers, and smoke-subject-headers.ts. Empty fixture directories yield [] and flow directly to it.each, removing every parameterized case. A missing or empty scripts/tests tree likewise yields zero smoke definitions, which the projection accepts and can render into empty authoritative artifacts. This is the vacuous-scanner failure class governed by CQ25-106 and lies outside the completed eslint-rules sweep.

Opened expand-barrel/run.ts, constants.ts, and the shared writer. runAll invokes runOne for each of three barrels; every runOne creates a fresh project, rescans packages, builds and immediately writes its own plan, and launches its own ESLint fix. A later analysis failure therefore follows persisted earlier edits, while files consuming multiple barrels undergo repeated transform/write cycles. The advertised bulk mode lacks a complete transaction plan.

Opened tools/lint-ratchet/src/governance/summary.ts and trend.ts. Both contain a tiny maxLength helper and padding assembly, but summary has five columns plus an optional directory dimension and two modes, while trend has eleven fixed columns, signed deltas, date/SHA formatting, and a different empty state. A configurable table abstraction would exceed the duplicated primitive logic without addressing demonstrated drift.

Opened debt-log-write.ts and searched every reference. appendValidatedDebtLogEntry is a six-line exported box-and-delegate wrapper whose only consumers are focused tests; production uses the batch API. Authored leaf 224 names this exact wrapper and already directs its deletion with the related compatibility shapes. The cut is fully covered.

promotionCandidates.title: Classify the below-Low "trivial" encounter tier as Musi policy

evidence.note: The module attributes the calculator to the 2024 DMG and describes only Low, Moderate, and High as XP-budget thresholds.
DifficultyRating places the application-added trivial label beside the three DMG threshold names without qualification.
The calculator assigns every encounter below the DMG Low threshold to trivial, making the policy executable.
The policy-protecting test calls the result simply trivial rather than identifying it as Musi policy.
The unqualified term is rendered directly to users alongside Low, Moderate, and High.
Repository policy requires rules behavior to be classified as SRD, named non-SRD source, or Musi policy.

promotionCandidates.problem: The calculator cites the DMG for encounter-building vocabulary, then silently adds a fourth user-visible tier below Low. Maintainers and users can reasonably read Trivial as DMG terminology, while the protecting test fails the repository's explicit provenance requirement.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Label the below-Low tier explicitly as Musi application policy in the rule comment and protecting test names; retain its behavior and user-facing label.

origins.originalTitle: The Musi-added 'trivial' difficulty tier is not labeled as application policy beside DMG vocabulary.
origins.rejectionReason: The Musi-added 'trivial' difficulty tier is not labeled as application policy beside DMG vocabulary.

priorPackOverlaps.residual: CQ25-95 requires every rules-facing slice to classify SRD, named external source, or Musi policy; this tier remains an unclassified live instance.

promotionCandidates.title: Slow-test Vitest config derives filesystem roots from a URL pathname

evidence.note: Passes URL.pathname directly into node:path before constructing all three slow-test project roots.
A comparable Vitest config converts import.meta.url with fileURLToPath before deriving its root.
Another root-pinning Vitest config uses the canonical fileURLToPath conversion.
The E2E environment demonstrates the same established repository idiom.

promotionCandidates.problem: URL.pathname is not a filesystem-path conversion: it retains percent encoding for characters such as spaces and yields URL-shaped drive paths on Windows. Because this value anchors every slow-test project, affected checkouts cannot locate their package roots.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Derive repoRoot with path.dirname(fileURLToPath(import.meta.url)), matching the other root-pinning configs.

promotionCandidates.title: Prototype source headers deny their now-registered advisory commands

evidence.note: The coverage config header says no check, subcommand, or advisory reads these artifact declarations.
The production command resolves config.coverage.artifacts, reads them, correlates them, and renders an advisory.
The module says no CLI or advisory is registered and a later task will wire it.
The module describes itself as library/test-only with no subcommand or advisory row.
The live handler registry exposes coverage-evidence, coverage-unused-exports, clone-candidates, and class-construction.

promotionCandidates.problem: In a large flat analyzer subsystem without a local MODULE.md at the pin, source headers are important ownership maps. Three headers still describe pre-wiring milestones and tell maintainers that four live advisory commands do not exist, inviting completed work to be re-planned and production behavior to be misclassified as test-only.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Rewrite only these milestone headers around current layering: core inventory/config modules remain finding-free libraries, while named command modules own the registered prototype surfaces.

origins.rejectionReason: Prototype milestone comments deny production command surfaces that now exist.

promotionCandidates.title: Schema-defined ability and spell-school vocabularies retain handwritten production inventories

evidence.note: abilityAbbreviationSchema is the closed canonical six-value ability contract.
SAVE_ABILITIES repeats the schema literals beside the canonical name map.
The homebrew monster form repeats the full ability inventory.
The ASI picker repeats the ability inventory while importing adjacent shared rules.
The NPC dialog synchronizes abbreviation and property-key arrays by positional index.
spellSchoolSchema is the canonical eight-value spell-school contract.
The homebrew editor repeats all eight schools and builds its validator Set from that private copy.
A school absent from the private inventory is silently normalized to evocation.
Neighboring spell UI already derives school options from spellSchoolSchema.options.

promotionCandidates.problem: Closed shared vocabularies are independently maintained by production consumers. Ability copies can omit or reorder an option, positional mappings can mislabel scores, and the homebrew spell copy can silently rewrite a shared-valid but locally absent school to Evocation.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Split by vocabulary during adjudication. Derive ability loops from abilityAbbreviationSchema.options or the canonical shared export, retaining explicit abbreviation-to-field maps where needed. Derive homebrew school options and parsing from spellSchoolSchema.options/safeParse and one typed label map.

promotionCandidates.title: Let multiclass characters choose among valid Unarmored Defense calculations

evidence.note: The seeded rule explicitly requires choosing which base-AC calculation to use.
The implementation silently selects the first matching Unarmored Defense class.
Tests establish Monk AC 15, Barbarian AC 13, and pin Barbarian-first multiclass AC to 13.
The sheet forwards class order into the shared computation without a choice input.
CharacterStats persists numeric AC but no selected AC calculation.
Encounter combat reads persisted stats.ac rather than the sheet calculation.

promotionCandidates.problem: Musi silently chooses the first eligible Unarmored Defense formula even though its seeded rule grants the player a choice. Multiclass row order can lower displayed AC, and the result can disagree with encounter AC because the two surfaces use different authorities.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Persist and validate the selected Unarmored Defense formula, pass it explicitly through shared AC calculation, and expose a sheet selector. Coordinate with computed-versus-persisted AC authority work and preserve a deterministic fallback for legacy rows.

promotionCandidates.title: Require fixture and smoke discovery to reject empty subject sets

evidence.note: The fixture enumerator returns every child directory without asserting that at least one case exists.
A representative suite passes the discovered array directly to it.each, so an empty result removes every fixture case.

evidence.measurement: 4 fixture-driven codemod test files call enumerateFixtures (`rg -l 'enumerateFixtures\(' scripts/codemods --glob '*.test.ts' | wc -l`)
evidence.note: The vacuous behavior affects concurrency-guard, expand-barrel, structured-logging-fix, and the two-kind tRPC fixture suite.
Smoke discovery returns [] when scripts/tests is missing and likewise for an existing empty directory.
Collection validates individual definitions and order uniqueness but has no non-empty precondition.
The empty definition set flows into both generated outputs.

promotionCandidates.problem: Two discovery-backed gates treat an empty subject population as success. Empty codemod fixture directories silently erase regression coverage, while an empty smoke tree can regenerate authoritative artifacts with no registered tests. Green output then means the scanner found nothing, not that subjects passed.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Add owner-local non-empty preconditions with subject-specific diagnostics before fixture arrays reach it.each and before smoke outputs are projected. Add focused empty-directory and missing-tree cases.

origins.originalTitle: fixture and smoke discovery accept an empty subject tree — routed as a low-priority scanner-hardening observation
origins.rejectionReason: fixture and smoke discovery accept an empty subject tree — routed as a low-priority scanner-hardening observation

priorPackOverlaps.residual: The ruling requires non-empty assertions for scanning guards; these codemod-fixture and smoke-subject scanners lie outside the completed eslint-rules sweep.
The prior decision rejected a shared assertion helper, not local scanner preconditions; this candidate keeps each reason local.

promotionCandidates.title: Build one complete plan for expand-barrel bulk mode

evidence.note: runOne creates a project, discovers every package file, builds one barrel-specific plan, and writes it immediately.
--all loops over independently analyzing and writing runOne calls instead of creating a single bulk plan.
Bulk mode repeats the operation for three known shared-package barrels.
Each barrel-specific invocation writes files and launches an ESLint import-fix pass immediately.

promotionCandidates.problem: The advertised bulk mode is sequential orchestration over single-barrel mutations. It repeatedly constructs projects and scans the repository, rewrites multiply affected files in stages, runs import fixing per barrel, and can leave earlier edits persisted when analysis of a later barrel fails.
promotionCandidates.proposedDirection: Analyze all existing known barrels in one project, apply their transforms to each source file in memory, validate the complete file plan, then call the shared writer once.

origins.originalTitle: expand-barrel --all executes per barrel instead of constructing one batch plan — lower-ranked codemod transactionality concern
origins.rejectionReason: expand-barrel --all executes per barrel instead of constructing one batch plan — lower-ranked codemod transactionality concern

coverageNotes: Audited exactly all 20 assigned cuts across lanes 04, 06, 07, 08, and 09; eight were promoted and twelve upheld.
No tests or builds were run. Work was limited to source/document reads, targeted rg searches, git status/diff inspection, and read-only SRD text extraction.
The branch differs from the audit target only in pack documentation; git diff over production, test, harness, workflow, and config surfaces returned no paths.

For the dice-decoder cut, CQ25-179 does not govern the narrow grammar as its cut text claimed; the disposition is still uphold because both consumers decode the same validated bare-formula contract and an extraction would be disproportionate.
The Unarmored Defense promotion treats the computed-versus-persisted AC authority mismatch as a sequencing dependency, not as a reason to suppress the player-choice mismatch.

The literal-inventory promotion sampled the concrete production ability copies in its evidence and the homebrew spell parser; it does not propose collapsing intentional subsets such as spellcasting-only abilities.
Wave 2 independently reconstructed the expand-barrel transactionality concern as retained finding L09-103, but no authored leaf in the supplied title corpus covers it.
